title: Siyum
hookLine: finishing a tractate is celebrated with a meal
tomorrow: Maimonides wrote ten chapters on coming back. where do they start?

lines: CAKE. PIZZA. A PLATE IN YOUR HANDS.
cards: Birthday cake. Pizza after the last game of the season. Somebody's grandmother pressing a plate into your hands at a graduation.
When something big ends, people reach for food. So what's on the table when you finish a tractate? A meal.
Bagels, cake, herring, whatever the community likes, set out after the last lines, the hadran and the Kaddish. It has a name, the seudat siyum, the meal of completion.

teach.h: ABAYE: A FEAST FOR SOMEONE ELSE.
teach.b: Where does that meal come from? One root is a line in the Talmud, in tractate Shabbat.
Abaye, a sage, says, in plain words: may I be rewarded, because whenever I saw a young scholar finish a tractate, I made a festive day for the rabbis. Notice whose finish it is. Not Abaye's own.
A young student's. Abaye throws the party for someone else's accomplishment, and counts that as something worth a reward. So the siyum meal isn't a trophy for the one who finished.
It's a table the whole community sits at, to say: this matters to all of us.

Something to tell a friend tonight: there's a custom on the day before Passover, when firstborn sons traditionally fast, that a siyum is held that morning, and the meal of completion releases the people who join it from the fast.

teach.h: A FAST TURNED INTO A FEAST.
teach.b: A finished book changes a fast day into a feast. And that's why the meal matters to the senses. You don't just know you finished.
Bread, salt, sweetness, voices at a crowded table. The learning was words on a page for weeks. At the end, it becomes something you can chew.

how: A siyum ends with a festive meal, the seudat siyum, open to everyone present; on the day before Passover synagogues often hold a siyum so that firstborns may join the meal instead of fasting.

o: completion: a finished tractate and a shared meal
the first page of a new tractate of the Talmud
a quiet fast kept after finishing a hard book

games.q: at the siyum table — tap the pairs.
p: a feast for a student's finish
a fast turned into a feast

s: the siyum meal is a reward the finisher eats alone

a siyum can release people from a fast

games.q: your friend quietly finished a hard online course and didn't tell anyone. what would Abaye do?
o: throw her a small celebration: her finish matters to everyone around her.
say nothing, since it was her goal and not yours.
wait until she finishes something bigger to celebrate.
games.why: Abaye made a festive day whenever a young scholar finished a tractate. celebrating someone else's finish was, to him, worth a reward.

practice: Take one small thing to eat, something you like: a piece of fruit, a cracker, a bite of something sweet. Eat it slowly, noticing the taste, the texture, the smell.
Let it stand for something you, or someone near you, finished lately.

wordCard.voice: Siyum. Hebrew for completion: finishing a tractate, and the meal where everyone tastes it together.

carryVoice: Your line: you finished a tractate, so set a table. Fifty of fifty: Berakhot is done.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Shabbat 118b–119a (Abaye: may I be rewarded, for when I saw a young scholar finish his tractate I made a festive day for the rabbis)
